summary: Interprets receipt 1bec110248d14e9e80aac0f8b8129f1c, the five-setting delay sweep, and uses it to replace the account's statement that the latency dependence was unmeasured. With 200 attempts per setting and a fresh store, transport and raft per case, the inversions were 0 at zero delay and then 96, 95, 100 and 94 at maximum current-term delays of 250 us, 500 us, 1 ms and 2 ms. Every comparison that requires zero inversions therefore holds at zero delay and is violated at all four other settings. The important result is the shape rather than any single number: the rate is not a gradual function of latency but jumps from none to about half between no delay and a quarter-millisecond maximum, and stays there across an eightfold increase, so the window is reached by ordinary scheduling jitter rather than by an unusually slow disk. The account keeps its violated conclusion and asserted defect, replaces the limitation about an unswept delay magnitude with the measured curve and its gaps (transition between 0 and 250 us not located, nothing above 2 ms, uniform distribution only), adds two counterevidence notes on how the saturation level depends on the start offset and on the artificial nature of the delay, and records the sweep as a fifth receipt from a separate experiment identifier whose attempt body, request shapes and inversion criterion match the frequency experiment. The submission validates with zero schema errors and requests no execution.
